# The notes form

<!-- Generated by `sigatla form --doc`. Edit sigatla/form.py, not this file. -->

Every source in an atlas has one notes file, `notes/<source-id>.json` (plus `notes/<source-id>.part-<k>.json` when a long source was read in parts). This page is the form for filling it in: the fields, the sections each note type needs, and the relations. The reading rules (faithfulness, marking interpretations, language) are in every reading pack that `sigatla pack` writes.

Machine-readable versions: [schema/](../schema/) (JSON Schema). A blank form for one note: `sigatla form <type>`; for a whole file: `sigatla form source`.

## The file

```json
{
 "source": {
  "title": "<title of the paper or deck>",
  "authors": "<as printed, or empty>",
  "year": "<four-digit year if printed, or empty>",
  "summary": "### Summary\n<problem, approach, main findings; the first sentence is a standalone one-line summary>\n\n### Contributions\n<a list>\n\n### How the notes are organized\n<one or two sentences>",
  "questions": [
   "<question about the whole source>"
  ]
 },
 "nodes": [
  {
   "id": "<source-id>.<slug>",
   "type": "concept",
   "title": "<at most about 8 words>",
   "short": "<one standalone sentence>",
   "body": "### What it is\n...\n\n### Intuition\n...\n\n### Why it matters here\n...",
   "questions": [
    "<question 1>",
    "<question 2>"
   ],
   "figures": [
    "<source-id>/<figure or slide id>"
   ],
   "pages": [
    1
   ],
   "links": [
    {
     "to": "<another note id>",
     "rel": "uses",
     "note": "<one or two sentences: how or why the relation holds>"
    }
   ]
  }
 ]
}
```

`source` describes the paper or deck as a whole and becomes the body of its planet. Its fields: `title`; `authors` and `year` as printed, or empty strings; `summary` in Markdown whose first sentence is the planet's one-line description; `questions` about the whole source.

## A note

| field | type | required | what goes in it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | `<source-id>.<slug>`, or `rw.<slug>` for related work; lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; unique; never change it once other notes link to it |
| `type` | enum | yes | concept, method, formula, design, result, limitation, data, example, related |
| `title` | string | yes | short and specific, at most about 8 words |
| `short` | string | yes | one standalone sentence, at most about 30 words; shown in tooltips and lists |
| `body` | Markdown | yes | `###` sections as in the skeleton for the type; $...$ and $$...$$ for math; no HTML; usually 120–400 words |
| `questions` | list of strings | yes (may be empty for related) | 2–4 exam, review or interview questions |
| `figures` | list of figure ids | yes (may be empty) | ids from the source's figure or slide list, at most 3; every figure shown in the body is listed here too |
| `pages` | list of integers | yes (may be empty) | PDF page numbers counted from 1 (not printed page numbers); for slides, the slide's page |
| `links` | list of {to, rel, note} | yes (may be empty) | relations to other notes, read as "this note REL target"; every link has a note |

## Sections of the body, by type

Write the headings in the notes' language (`sigatla form <type> --lang vi` prints Vietnamese ones). Leave out a section the source gives nothing for, rather than filling it with guesses.

### `concept`: an idea, definition or problem

```markdown
### What it is
...

### Intuition
...

### Why it matters here
...
```

### `method`: a method, algorithm, model or architecture

```markdown
### Inputs and outputs
...

### How it works
...

### Why it matters here
...
```

### `formula`: an equation shown in the source; explain every symbol

```markdown
### Formula
$$ display math (LaTeX) $$

### Symbols
- $x$: what it is (one item per symbol)

### Meaning
...

### Why this form
...
```

### `design`: a design choice of a study, or a rule the source recommends, with the reason

```markdown
### What was chosen
...

### What it rules out
...

### Why
...
```

### `result`: a finding with the numbers as reported

```markdown
### Numbers
| setting | value |
| --- | --- |
| ... | as reported |

### Setting
...

### What it shows
...
```

### `limitation`: a limitation, threat to validity or open question

```markdown
### What it is
...

### What it affects
...

### What could address it
...
```

### `data`: a dataset, benchmark or model checkpoint

```markdown
### Facts
...

### How it is used
...
```

### `example`: a worked example

```markdown
### Setup
...

### Steps
...

### Outcome
...

### Lesson
...
```

### `related`: another work the source cites (id `rw.<slug>`); it has no links of its own

```markdown
### Citation
...

### What the source says about it
...

### Relation to this source
...
```

## Relations

A link is read as "this note REL target". Its `note` says concretely how or why the relation holds, in one or two sentences.

| rel | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `part_of` | is a component or step of the target |
| `uses` | needs or applies the target |
| `extends` | builds on the target and changes or generalizes it |
| `motivates` | gives the reason for the target |
| `contrasts` | differs from the target in an instructive way |
| `measures` | quantifies the target |
| `tests` | is an experiment or check that examines the target |
| `limits` | restricts where the target holds or how well it works |
| `supports` | is evidence for the target |
| `refutes` | is evidence against the target |
| `cites` | refers to the target without a stronger relation |
| `frames` | sets the context for the target |
| `complements` | covers a different side of the same topic |

## Other files

- `notes/_shared.json` (`sigatla pack --connect`): `axis` (the central question, the sun of the map), `nodes` (shared concepts, ids `shared.<slug>`), `links` (`from`, `to`, `rel`, `note`) across sources.
- `notes/_qa.json`: saved questions and answers, a list of `{node, q, a, source, at}` (plus `link` or `path` when the question was about a link or a path).

## Before you finish

- `sigatla check` reports 0 errors, and no hints for the notes you wrote.
- Every number comes from the source; every explanation beyond it starts with the interpretation marker ("Interpretation:", "Diễn giải:").
- Every figure id and link target exists; every link has a note.
- `sigatla build`, then open `site/index.html` and look at a few notes.
